title: Building Evidence in Miniature
paras: In a specialist model workshop, Amira builds miniature machines for courtroom demonstrations. Her latest commission, intended for a criminal [[prosecution|prosecution]] concerning an unguarded factory press, begins not with cutting timber but with checking measurements. Photographs establish the operator’s [[posture|posture]], while maintenance drawings reveal which components could move. The model must distinguish documented facts from assumptions without pretending to reproduce the accident itself.

Before construction, Amira must [[conceive|conceive]] a mechanism that makes the press’s hydraulic action visible. Her [[liberal|liberal]] approach allows technicians to propose unconventional materials, but disagreement over glass and plastic produces a [[deadlock|deadlock]]. They resolve it by testing both: transparent plastic withstands handling better, whereas glass provides a clearer view of the liquid travelling through a narrow [[capillary|capillary]].

The resulting design combines a plastic housing with a protected glass tube. Assembly is [[laborious|laborious]]: each joint is sealed, left overnight, then inspected under a lamp for leakage. Initially, the tiny pump produces only a [[feeble|feeble]] movement of coloured water. Rather than increase the pressure and distort the demonstration, Amira reduces friction in the miniature piston, allowing the mechanism to operate at the intended setting.

During its [[maiden|maiden]] demonstration, the finished model is filmed beside a ruler, so reviewers can judge its scale and speed. Labels identify altered dimensions, and a separate diagram explains why miniature fluid systems behave differently from industrial equipment. Such qualifications improve [[clarity|clarity]] rather than weaken the exhibit: the final object shows how the machine works while leaving questions of responsibility to the court.
zh: 在一家专业模型工坊里，阿米拉制作供法庭演示使用的微缩机器。她最新接到的委托涉及一宗刑事起诉，案件与工厂里一台缺少防护装置的压力机有关。制作并非从切割木材开始，而是先核对尺寸。照片用于确定操作人员的姿势，维修图纸则显示哪些部件能够运动。模型必须区分有记录支持的事实与推测，不能佯称自己重现了事故本身。
动工之前，阿米拉必须构思一种能直观展示压力机液压作用的机制。她思想开放，允许技术人员提出采用非常规材料，但大家在玻璃和塑料的选择上产生分歧，工作陷入僵局。他们通过分别测试两种材料解决问题：透明塑料更经得起搬动，而玻璃能让人更清楚地看到液体流过细窄毛细管的过程。
最终的设计将塑料外壳与一根受到保护的玻璃管结合起来。组装十分费时费力：每个接头都要密封，静置一夜，再放到灯下检查是否渗漏。起初，微型泵只能让有色水产生微弱的流动。阿米拉没有提高压力，以免演示失真，而是减小微型活塞的摩擦，使机构能够在预定设置下运转。
首次演示时，工作人员把一把尺子放在成品模型旁边进行录像，以便审核人员判断其比例和运行速度。标签标明经过调整的尺寸，另附的示意图则解释微型流体系统的表现为何不同于工业设备。这些限定说明不仅没有削弱展品的作用，反而使展示更加清晰：最终制成的模型说明了机器如何运作，同时将责任归属问题留给法庭裁决。

q.s: Amira starts cutting timber before checking the measurements for her latest model.
q.why: 首段明确说先核对尺寸，而非切割木材。

q.s: The workshop had used transparent plastic in earlier courtroom models.
q.why: 文中未说明此前的法庭模型用过何种材料。

q.s: The finished model has labels identifying dimensions that have been altered.
q.why: 末段明确说标签标明经过调整的尺寸。
